definitions.explanation: A collection of short essays by the monk {兼好法師|けんこうほうし} (Yoshida Kenkō), written around 1330. Its 243 sections range over impermanence, taste, manners, and odd anecdotes, and it is one of the three great classical essay collections along with {枕草子|まくらのそうし} and {方丈記|ほうじょうき}.

examples.english: Essays in Idleness is a famous collection of essays.

examples.english: Essays in Idleness is full of wisdom about life that still rings true today.

notes:
The title comes from the first words, つれづれなるままに ("having nothing to do"), and つれづれ has kept that sense of idle leisure in modern Japanese.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- つれづれなるままに、⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ぐらし⟦{硯|すずり}→硯：06124_suzuri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{向|む}かひて: "With nothing to do, facing my inkstone all day" — the opening line
- ⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧のことにも、⟦{先達|せんだつ}→先達：20598_sendatsu⟧はあらまほしき{事|こと}なり: "Even in small matters, one wants a guide" — often quoted
- {兼好法師|けんこうほうし}: the author, also called {吉田兼好|よしだけんこう}

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kenkō praised the beauty of things that are incomplete or passing, such as cherry blossoms before they bloom or after they fall. This taste became a pillar of the Japanese aesthetic.
